objective: five real-data cases beating every mandatory applicable competitor on net_cost

structural_finding: FIVE competitor acquisition rules provably collapse to disagreement-gated sampling in the two-model binary task (Model Picker, Online LLM Picker, variance minimisation, Xu acquisition-only, Model Selector). Instance-level acquisition has nothing to work with here, so any comparison is about query-rate scheduling and deployment economics.
stop_reason: Pre-registered rule fired: lost to GatedDeploymentStop on both powered cases (rialto +1.852 [+0.989,+3.394]; openml_ldpa +9.585 [+5.320,+14.678]).
key_finding: P3b is not the state of the art for this task. Gated deployment (ICML 2021) is cheaper on both powered datasets and far more label-efficient (30.8 vs 159.2 labels on rialto), so the B3+ result is a win over a weak baseline.
correction: An earlier update recorded 'PROGRAMME STOPPED'. That was an overreach. The pre-registered economic-stop rule governed only EconomicStop versus certificate stops. P7s has now been compared against the applicable implemented suite on exposed Rialto and OpenML-LDPA loss paths. It beats Gated deployment by 57.751 net-cost units on LDPA but loses to the Model Picker and Model Selector adapters by 46.485 and 43.392, respectively; on Rialto it loses to Gated by 3.847. The two loss-preserving binary label encodings give identical results. This replay uses artificial labels/predictions reconstructed from real loss paths, so it is not an authentic prediction-stream evaluation or independent confirmation. The SOTA gate remains unmet.
